title: 401 login error gives wrong guidance vs Expo's 'wrong credentials / contact lab to reset password'
expoEvidence: driver-login.tsx:48-49 — `} else if (status === 401) { Alert.alert('بيانات غير صحيحة', 'تواصل مع المعمل لإعادة تعيين كلمة المرور'); }`
detail: On a 401 (bad password) Expo always overrides with a fixed, actionable message telling the driver to contact the lab to reset their password — auth accounts are lab-created, so this guidance matters. Flutter relies on the generic ApiException message; if the backend sends no message it shows 'session expired, log in again' which is the wrong meaning for a failed login (the user IS on the login screen). The lab-reset hint is never shown on 401.
reason: Could not refute — the behavior is genuinely absent in Flutter, and the gap is worse than the auditor described. Expo (mobile-worker/app/(auth)/driver-login.tsx:48-49) ALWAYS overrides a 401 with fixed Arabic guidance 'بيانات غير صحيحة' / 'تواصل مع المعمل لإعادة تعيين كلمة المرور', and also specially handles 429 (line 46-47). Flutter login_screen.dart:63-65 only does `showSnack(context, e.message)` with the raw ApiException message. I confirmed there is NO override anywhere: auth_interceptor.dart:28-31 + 56 explicitly EXCLUDE /auth/login from the 401-refresh/onSessionExpired path, so a login 401 propagates straight to the screen; auth_controller.dart:44-57 and auth_repository.dart:16-34 just rethrow ApiException.fromDio with no per-status remapping. Decisive: the backend login endpoint (backend/src/auth/auth.service.ts:227,230) throws UnauthorizedException('Invalid phone or password') — an ENGLISH string. api_exception.dart:_extractMessage (lines 30-31) prefers the backend message, so an Arabic-speaking driver entering a wrong password sees raw English 'Invalid phone or password', never the Arabic 'contact the lab to reset your password' hint. (The auditor's 'session expired' fallback only triggers if the backend sends no message, which it does not here.) No 429-specific message exists in Flutter either. Severity medium: auth still functions and rejects bad credentials, but the user-facing guidance is wrong/untranslated and the actionable lab-reset hint is lost.

The Flutter driver login (apps/driver/lib/screens/login_screen.dart:63-65) catches ApiException and passes e.message straight to showSnack with NO rate-limit override. For a 429, e.message resolves to the shared generic fallback in packages/daari_core/lib/src/api/api_exception.dart:52 -> 'محاولات كثيرة. انتظر قليلاً ثم حاول مجدداً.' ('wait a little'), with no '15 minute' figure. title: After successful reset, Flutter routes to /login instead of auto-logging in to home

detail: The screen calls the repository directly instead of the AuthController.resetPasswordAndLogin() helper, so the in-memory auth state stays unauthenticated even though tokens are saved to storage. Because authControllerProvider is never set to authenticated, the router redirect at router.dart:44 will NOT auto-forward /login to /home, so the user is dropped on the login screen and must manually sign in — regressing Expo's seamless auto-login-to-home after reset. reason: Confirmed real gap. Expo (mobile-worker/app/(auth)/forgot.tsx:76-80) persists fresh tokens, hydrates the auth store, and router.replace's to home — user is auto-signed-in. Flutter forgot_screen.dart:68-75 calls authRepositoryProvider.resetPassword() directly then context.go('/login'). resetPassword (auth_repository.dart:83-102) saves tokens and returns me() but never updates AuthController state. The dedicated AuthController.resetPasswordAndLogin() (auth_controller.dart:60-74) which would set state=authenticated is NEVER called. Because authControllerProvider stays unauthenticated, AuthState.isAuthenticated (auth_state.dart:12-13) is false, so the router redirect (router.dart:42-44) does NOT forward /login to /home — the !loggedIn branch (line 43) keeps the user on /login. Searched the screen, auth_repository, auth_controller, auth_state, router.dart, providers.dart, providers/core_providers (via imports), and login_screen — nowhere re-syncs auth state after reset. User is dropped on /login and must manually sign in, regressing Expo's seamless auto-login-to-home. HIGH: auth flow regression forcing re-authentication.

title: Periodic offline-queue flush is Home-tab-scoped, not app-wide
expoEvidence: app/_layout.tsx:60-66 drains the queue on mount and on a 60s interval at the ROOT layout level: `flush().catch(()=>{}); const t = setInterval(()=>{ flush()... }, 60_000);` — runs regardless of which screen is showing.
detail: In Expo the queue drains every 60s anywhere in the app (the timer lives in _layout). In Flutter the periodic drain only runs while the Home tab is mounted; if the driver stays on task-detail / cash / walkin (offline then reconnects) for over a minute, queued mutations are not flushed until they return to Home. Same flush logic, narrower trigger scope.
reason: Real gap, not refuted. Expo runs the 60s periodic flush + mount flush at the ROOT layout (app/_layout.tsx:60-66), so it drains app-wide on any screen. In Flutter the periodic Timer.periodic(60s) and the initial flush live entirely in HomeScreen.initState (home_screen.dart:38, 41-42) and are cancelled in dispose (line 47). I checked the shared core (offline_queue.dart only exposes flush(), it does not self-schedule; isOnlineProvider/offlineQueueProvider in core_providers.dart are just streams/providers with no flush trigger), main.dart, router.dart, home_shell.dart, and providers.dart — none host an app-level periodic or background drain. The other flush call sites (task_detail_screen.dart:119, walkin_screen.dart:299/495) are per-submit post-mutation flushes, not background periodic drains. Flutter does ADD a reconnect-driven flush via ref.listen(isOnlineProvider) at home_screen.dart:125-126, but that listener is registered in HomeScreen.build and only fires while HomeScreen is mounted — same narrow scope. So if the driver stays on task-detail/cash/walkin/earnings (each a separate route that unmounts HomeScreen) for over a minute after reconnecting, queued mutations are not drained until they return to Home. Medium (not high): mutations persist in SQLite and are not lost — they flush on next Home visit or per-submit — so this is delayed-flush, not data-loss/double-submit.
